title: Throughput-aware microbatch ceiling and KV-prefix caching sensitivity study
creator: Anjali Mehra
description: Objective: quantify end-user quality impact vs latency/cost when changing microbatch ceilings and KV-prefix caching parameters. We want to establish safe operating envelopes and automated alert thresholds so Console Optimize can recommend configs without causing silent quality regressions.
acceptance_criteria: Run N=8 controlled experiments covering microbatch_size (1,8,16,32), batching_deadline_ms (5,20,50) and kv_cache_ttl (0,30,300s) across two model families (redwood-3B and open-7B).

Produce a latency/cost vs quality contour map for each model + request profile with P50/P95 latency, tokens/sec, cost-per-1M-tokens, and per-prompt quality delta (embedding-similarity and task pass-rate).
Define automated rollback thresholds: explicit tradeoffs where quality drop >1.5% absolute OR task pass-rate drop >2% will be flagged as high-risk for recommendations.
Submit report and recommendation RFC for Console Optimize integration and one canary rollout plan for Dedicated pools.
tasks: Assemble eval corpus: production trace samples (10k sessions), curated regression set (1k prompts), adversarial edgecases (200 prompts)
Implement experiment harness matrix in runtime-harness (PR: github.com/redwood/runtime-harness/pull/412)
Run baseline calibration with current prod config and save metrics to s3://redwood-evals/ENG-57321/baseline
Run full factorial sweep and collect latency, cost, and quality metrics
Analyze results and generate contour plots + per-prompt outlier list
Draft RFC and rollout playbook for Console Optimize and Dedicated autoscaler changes
risks: Small but systematic quality regressions may only appear in rare prompt patterns — need large enough sample to detect 1% effects.
Cost estimates are model- and region-dependent; ensure we run experiments on both us-west and eu-central pools.
Autoscaler interactions: aggressive batch ceilings could starve small tenants or violate SLOs if not constrained per-tenant.
decisions: Use embedding-cosine (sentence-transformer-based) + task pass-rate as primary quality signal for this study.
Treat kv_cache_ttl=0 as explicit 'disabled' baseline; include 30s and 300s TTLs to capture warm vs long-lived caches.
Report both absolute and relative quality deltas and include per-prompt examples for any >2% regression buckets.
updates: 2026-02-03: Corpus assembled (Anjali). 10k sessions anonymized and sampled into three buckets by length.
